title: Oven Scrambled Eggs
directions: Divide butter among 4 - 13" x 9" x 2" bk. dishes; Combine eggs & salt; mix well.
Gradually stir in milk. Pour evenly into bk. dishes.
Bake, uncovered @ 350° for 10 min; stir. Bake 10-15 min. more until eggs are set. Serve immediately.
notes: Marked 'lg. quantity recipe' at top right.
Yield 100 servings.
Photo 368 is a full re-shot of this same card.
raw_text:
lg. quantity recipe
Oven scrambled eggs.
2 c butter melted
100 eggs, beaten
3 tbsp. salt.
2 1/2 qts. milk.
Divide butter among 4 - 13" x 9" x 2" bk. dishes; Combine eggs
& salt; mix well. Gradually stir in milk. Pour evenly
into bk. dishes. Bake, uncovered @ 350° for 10 min; stir. Bake

title: Oyster Stew
ingredients: 1 cup (250 mL) celery very finely diced
1/2 cup (125 mL) white wine or dry sherry
directions: In a large saucepan melt 1/2 cup butter, add vegetables, stir until vegetables are well coated with butter. Cover, simmer 20 minutes over very low heat, stirring once or twice.

In a saucepan over medium heat melt 1/4 cup (50 mL) butter, add flour, stir cook for 1 minute. Add milk and cream, stir until smooth and creamy. Add sauce to vegetables. Salt and pepper to taste. Mix thoroughly and set aside.

Bring to boil minced clams in their juice. Add oysters to clams, then add wine or sherry. Cook over low heat for 10 minutes. DO NOT BOIL. When very hot pour into creamed vegetable mixture. Stir over low heat. DO NOT BOIL.
Serve soup in a deep plate or soup bowl. Sprinkle with paprika.
notes: Printed newspaper/magazine clipping with holly decoration (Christmas feature).
Intro text: 'Several years ago Mme. Benoit published this recipe from Canadian Pacific's inaugural transcontinental train journey. It was served to John A. MacDonald's guests on that historic run.'

OYSTER STEW
Several years ago Mme. Benoit published this recipe from
Canadian Pacific's inaugural transcontinental train journey. It was
served to John A. MacDonald's guests on that historic run.

2          carrots, shredded                  2
6-8        green onions, finely minced        6-8
1          leek, thinly sliced                1
1/4 cup    unsalted butter                    50 mL
1/2 cup    flour                              125 mL
2 cups     2% milk                            500 mL
2 cups     cereal cream                       500 mL
           Salt and pepper to taste
1          can (5 oz./142 mL) clams, minced   1
2 cups     fresh oysters                      500 mL
1/2 cup    white wine or dry sherry           125 mL
           Paprika
In a large saucepan melt 1/2 cup butter, add vegetables, stir until vegetables are well coated with butter. Cover, simmer 20 minutes over very low heat, stirring once or twice.
In a saucepan over medium heat melt 1/4 cup (50 mL) butter, add flour, stir cook for 1 minute. Add milk and cream, stir until smooth and creamy. Add sauce to vegetables.
Salt and pepper to taste. Mix thoroughly and set aside.
Bring to boil minced clams in their juice. Add oysters to clams, then add wine or sherry. Cook over low heat for 10 minutes. DO NOT BOIL. When very hot pour into creamed vegetable mixture. Stir over low heat. DO NOT BOIL.
Serve soup in a deep plate or soup bowl. Sprinkle with paprika.

title: Salmon Loaf
directions: Dissolve gelatin in water.
Cut French bread in half & hollow out the middle for your bread crumbs, leaving 1 1/2" crust.
Combine gelatin, salmon, cheese, ketchup, mayonnaise, pepper, mustard, pimento, pickle, & bread crumbs & mix well.
Fill the French loaf c̄ the salmon mixture. Chill in fridge before slicing.
This loaf freezes well.
notes: Written on a sheet of paper (not a card); a stuffed French-bread salmon loaf served chilled and sliced.
Ditto marks: '3 " mayonnaise' = 3 tbsp; '1/4 " dry mustard' = 1/4 tsp.
raw_text:
Salmon Loaf.                  3 tbsp. ketchup.
1 tbsp gelatin                3 "  mayonnaise
1/2 c cold water              1/4 tsp. pepper
1 loaf French bread.          1/4 "  dry mustard
1 1/2 c. soft bread crumbs.   3 tbsp. pimento
2 x 7 1/2 oz. tins salmon     1/2 c sweet pickle.
4 oz. cream cheese.
Dissolve gelatin in water. Cut French bread
in half & hollow out the middle for your bread
crumbs, leaving 1 1/2" crust. Combine gelatin,
salmon, cheese, ketchup, mayonnaise, pepper,
mustard, pimento, pickle, & bread crumbs &
mix well. Fill the French loaf c̄ the salmon
mixture. Chill in fridge before slicing.
This loaf freezes well.
